correctness.rationale: A deleted matched pair with both endpoints labeled 2 gives weight four and perfectly defends every zero vertex. Any function with at most one 2 forces all other vertices in that 2-vertex's bipartition class to be positive. This excludes weights below four; at weight four, the n=3 boundary with one 2 would leave its matched opposite vertex undefended. Hence an optimum has two 2s, one in each class, and their deleted-matching indices must coincide. Exhaustive checks over 5,380,749 labelings for n=3..7 corroborate the proof.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a standard dense regular bipartite family whose defining deleted matching gives each vertex a unique opposite-side nonneighbor. The theorem proves that this structure exactly controls all optimal perfect Roman functions: the invariant is constant at four while the complete optimum family is in bijection with the deleted matching. This is a natural exact regular-family result and a full optimizer classification, not an arbitrary finite slice.
